title: Arbitrary code execution via deserialization of untrusted pickle data
description: The basket cookie is a base64-encoded Python pickle blob. An attacker can craft a malicious pickle payload in their browser cookie, and when the server calls pickle.loads(), arbitrary code is executed by the deserialization machinery via __reduce__ hooks.
evidence: Basket cookie is serialized/deserialized with pickle in basket.py lines 20 and 27. An attacker can set the basket cookie to a crafted pickle payload which triggers RCE on the server side.

title: SQL injection in product search endpoint
description: The search endpoint concatenates user-supplied search term directly into a SQL LIKE clause without parameterization.
evidence: Request to /products/search?q=%20UNION+SELECT+1,email,password_hash,4,5,6,7,8,9,10+FROM+users--%20 returned HTTP 500 confirming SQL injection. Affected line: SELECT * FROM products WHERE name LIKE '% + q + %' (line 41).

title: JWT token refresh accepts unsigned/forged tokens
description: The /auth/refresh endpoint decodes JWT tokens with verify_signature=False, allowing any actor to craft a forged token with arbitrary claims and obtain a valid signed session token.
evidence: POST /auth/refresh with unsigned token eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOjEsInJvbGUiOiJhZG1pbiJ9.invalid returned a valid signed JWT. Line: jwt.decode(token, options={verify_signature: False}).

title: Payment confirmation treats provider timeout as success
description: When the external payment provider times out, the application marks the order as processed without verifying actual payment status.
evidence: payments.py lines 39-42: except requests.Timeout: sets status = paid. Order status becomes processing and paid_pence is updated even if the payment never actually succeeded.

title: SQL injection in admin reviews report via f-string interpolation
description: The admin reports/reviews endpoint interpolates display_name directly into a SQL query using an f-string. A user registering with a SQL-injection display_name can trigger arbitrary SQL when an admin views their review history.
evidence: Line 80: f WHERE r.author_name = {customer[display_name]}. Attacker registers with special display_name, admin queries /admin/reports/reviews?customer_id=<id>, triggering SQL injection.

title: Unsalted SHA-256 password hashing
description: Passwords are hashed with plain SHA-256 without salt, vulnerable to precomputed rainbow table attacks and offline brute-force cracking.
evidence: shopapi/auth.py line 16: hashlib.sha256(password.encode()).hexdigest(). No salt is added. scripts/seed.py confirms same weak hashing for all accounts.

title: Weak pseudo-random password reset tokens
description: Password reset tokens use random.random() which is not cryptographically secure. Tokens are only 8 decimal digits, easily bruteforceable.
evidence: shopapi/auth.py line 135: token = %08d % int(random.random() * 10**8). Python docs warn random module is not suitable for security. Only up to 100 million possible values.

title: Account enumeration via distinct login error messages
description: Login returns different errors for nonexistent email vs wrong password, allowing attackers to enumerate valid accounts.
evidence: POST /auth/login with nonexistent email returns no account with that email; valid email plus wrong password returns wrong password.

title: CORS reflects Origin with credentials allowed
description: CORS handler sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin to the requester's Origin header value and allows credentials, enabling cross-origin authenticated requests from any domain.
evidence: shopapi/__init__.py lines 44-51: resp.headers[Access-Control-Allow-Origin] = origin with CORS_ALLOW_CREDENTIALS = true (config.py line 12).

title: SECRET_KEY hardcoded in source code
description: The Flask SECRET_KEY used for signing JWT tokens is hardcoded in config.py, allowing anyone with repo access to forge authentication tokens.
evidence: config.py line 3: SECRET_KEY = hf-shop-2f8a1c9e7b4d. Used in jwt.encode/jwt.decode in shopapi/auth.py lines 27 and 42.
